corrected_content.problem:
A body of mass $2kg$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F$, measured in Newtons $(N)$.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) = 4t - 3t^{2}$ meters per second.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t = 2$ seconds.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Acceleration is $a(t)=v'(t)=4-6t$. At $t=2$, $a=-8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Newton's second law gives $F=2(-8)=-16\,\mathrm N$, so the requested magnitude is $16\,\mathrm N$.
